neighbours.label: a change of bodily or physical state that comes with age or time (becomes, menopause, eventually replaced), the 'change' side of the keep/maintain distinction
fire: As we grow older, our bones become more brittle.
Over time, the paint becomes faded and cracked.
After menopause, many women lose bone density.
With age, the skin becomes thinner and less elastic.
Old batteries eventually need to be replaced.
As the years pass, hearing gradually becomes weaker.
Once puberty begins, the voice becomes deeper.
In late autumn, the leaves turn brown and fall.
quiet: Our bones are made mostly of calcium and collagen.
The paint on the fence is dark green.
Many women visit their doctor for a yearly checkup.
The skin is the largest organ of the body.
The batteries are kept in a drawer in the kitchen.
Hearing depends on tiny hair cells in the inner ear.
The voice is produced by vibrating vocal cords.
The leaves of the oak are broad and lobed.

notes: - pole suppresses keep/maintain. Probe: 'with age ... becomes' 0.582, menopause 0.513, 'before they are replaced' 0.269, 'time to upgrade' 0.083; static descriptions 0.015/0.022/0.017; leak 'maintain a steady temperature' 0.277.
